extracted.intended_audience: Department of the Treasury and other federal regulators; state bankers associations, member banks, and policy stakeholders involved in notice-and-comment on the GENIUS Act NPRM
extracted.subtask_short: requesting extension of NPRM comment deadline
extracted.subtask_description: Drafting a joint association comment letter asking Treasury to extend the public comment deadline for an NPRM that is substantively dependent on a separate agency's pending proposed rule (the OCC GENIUS Proposal), explaining grounds and proposing a specific remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: NPRM is substantively tethered to OCC GENIUS Proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: The NPRM is substantively tethered to the OCC GENIUS Proposal; Treasury's proposal is directly contingent on the OCC's final framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the NPRM defines the 'Federal regulatory framework' to encompass OCC interpretations or regulations, Treasury should recognize that comments on the NPRM cannot be fully informed until the OCC finalizes its rule. When an NPRM is materially dependent on another agency's pending rule, the comment period should account for that dependency (e.g., by extending the deadline or coordinating timing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Federal regulatory framework' includes OCC interpretations/regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Treasury's NPRM defines the 'Federal regulatory framework' to include 'any interpretations [of the GENIUS Act], or regulations thereunder issued by the OCC and published in the Federal Register.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a proposed regulation explicitly ties its operative federal standard to future or unsettled interpretations/regulations from another agency, the proposing agency should allow stakeholders the opportunity to comment after those interpretations/regulations are finalized or otherwise ensure coordination so that commenters can evaluate the full federal baseline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency acknowledgement of contingent reliance on another pending proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Treasury expressly acknowledges that it 'took into consideration the OCC's proposed rule' and that the OCC's rule 'may change at the final rule stage' and that Treasury 'may modify the final text' to account for such changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the agency itself states the proposed rule was developed in consideration of a separate pending proposal that may change, this is a reason to extend the comment period so stakeholders can comment on the final, aligned frameworks rather than on provisional text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive comments cannot be fully developed until the OCC rule is final
rubrics_metrics.description: Until the OCC's rule is final, Treasury's proposal for assessing state-level regulatory regimes is necessarily provisional, and substantive comment on whether proposed state-level standards meet or exceed the Federal regulatory framework cannot be fully developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should ensure commenters have a stable factual and regulatory basis for substantive comments; where material uncertainty exists because a related rule is pending, the comment period should be adjusted to permit meaningful, informed input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk to state legislative activity from simultaneous action
rubrics_metrics.description: Because state laws pertaining to state qualified stablecoin issuers must adhere to Treasury's 'substantially similar' architecture (which is dependent on the OCC's GENIUS regulation), simultaneous or rushed federal actions risk causing states to pass laws that would later be judged insufficient by the Stablecoin Certification Review Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulators should avoid timelines that create pressure for states to adopt premature or incompatible legislation; coordination or timing adjustments (such as extensions) can reduce the risk of creating downstream compliance problems and the need for subsequent amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies should signal that getting it right is more important than speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Treasury must send a strong signal to state legislatures that getting it right is more important than moving quickly to pass laws that might have to be amended later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond procedural adjustments, agencies should use their communications and scheduling to discourage rushed state action and emphasize the value of alignment and accuracy over rapid enactment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requested procedural remedy: 60-day extension tied to OCC final rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The Associations request that Treasury extend the deadline for public comments on the NPRM by 60 days after the issuance of a final rule by the OCC implementing the GENIUS Act for entities subject to the OCC's jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asking for an extension tied to a related agency's final action, specify a concrete remedy (here, '60 days after OCC final rule') so agencies can evaluate the request and implement coordinated timing adjustments.
